lemon-hill.description: Lemon Hill is East Fairmount Park's historic mansion and hilltop landscape, currently closed to public use during post-Fan-Festival breakdown and restoration planning.
lemon-hill.location: Use the mansion pin at 1 Lemon Hill Drive. The hill sits above Kelly Drive in East Fairmount Park and is separate from Belmont Plateau, Memorial Hall and the West Park attractions.
lemon-hill.parking: Do not drive to Lemon Hill while the park is closed. Event breakdown and restoration work can control Lemon Hill Drive, nearby park roads and curb access; choose another Fairmount Park destination until the operator lifts the closure.
lemon-hill.hours: Lemon Hill park is currently closed to the public for FIFA Fan Festival breakdown. Mansion access is also by scheduled visit rather than general park hours. Check the official page before traveling.
lemon-hill.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom available while the Lemon Hill area and mansion are closed. Plan facilities at a confirmed-open destination elsewhere in Fairmount Park.
lemon-hill.fees: There is no general public visit while the closure is in effect. Future mansion tours or programs may require reservations or admission; use the official schedule when access resumes.
lemon-hill.accessibility: Closure fencing and work areas make the current visit unavailable. When the site reopens, confirm the mansion entrance and step-free route because a historic hilltop building and sloping grounds do not provide uniform access.
lemon-hill.dogs: Do not bring pets into the closed area. When ordinary park access resumes, the City's six-foot leash rule will apply outdoors, while the historic house may keep separate animal restrictions.
lemon-hill.family: Skip Lemon Hill as a family destination until the closure is lifted. The City has announced future playground, restoration, tree, lighting and accessibility improvements, but opening dates and finished amenities are not yet published.
lemon-hill.need: This is a real temporary closure, not simply a mansion-hours issue. Recheck the official Lemon Hill page and City improvement updates before making the hill the purpose of a trip.

belmont-plateau.description: Belmont Plateau is West Fairmount Park's broad skyline overlook and open recreation landscape, with picnic space, sports fields and connections toward the Trolley Trail.
belmont-plateau.location: Navigate to Belmont Plateau on Belmont Mansion Drive, not the broad Fairmount Park pin. The skyline lawn is in West Fairmount Park, north of the Mann Center and west of the Schuylkill River.
belmont-plateau.parking: Use legal spaces serving Belmont Mansion Drive and the plateau, then follow posted event restrictions. Roots Picnic and other large events can close roads, reserve lots and change rideshare or pedestrian approaches.
belmont-plateau.hours: Use the open lawn and trail connections during daylight; City parks have a 10 p.m. curfew and trails are dawn to dusk. Permitted events, field reservations, gates and maintenance can control the plateau independently.
belmont-plateau.restrooms: Do not count on a permanently open restroom at the overlook. Restroom access may be tied to an event, permitted field or seasonal facility, so confirm before settling in for a long picnic.
belmont-plateau.fees: Ordinary overlook, lawn and trail access is free. Ticketed festivals, permitted gatherings, vendors and reserved sports use are separate.
belmont-plateau.accessibility: The primary arrival reaches a broad open plateau, but grass, slopes, curb transitions, event barriers and natural-surface trail connections vary. Confirm the event layout when visiting during a festival.
belmont-plateau.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary open park areas under the City's six-foot leash rule. Keep pets out of active fields, event-controlled areas and any posted animal-free zones.
belmont-plateau.family: The skyline view and open lawn work for a picnic or short family stop, but this is not a fenced playground. Bring shade and water, supervise near roads and fields, and verify restroom availability.
belmont-plateau.need: Belmont Plateau changes character during major festivals and sports events. Check the City event calendar, road restrictions and weather before relying on a normal parking or picnic setup.

fairmount-water-works.description: Fairmount Water Works is the free watershed education center and historic riverfront complex below the Philadelphia Museum of Art, with exhibits and outdoor Schuylkill views.
fairmount-water-works.location: Navigate to 640 Waterworks Drive below the art museum. The entrance is at river level beside the Schuylkill, not at the Rocky Steps or the upper museum plaza.
fairmount-water-works.parking: The operator lists free two-hour parking along Waterworks Drive. Spaces and vehicle access can change for events, flooding and road closures, so use SEPTA, PHLASH or a backup garage when the riverfront is busy.
fairmount-water-works.hours: The interpretive center is open Wednesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Outdoor riverfront paths may be accessible more broadly, but exhibits, restrooms and staff follow building hours.
fairmount-water-works.restrooms: Use visitor facilities during interpretive-center hours. Do not assume the building is open on Sunday through Tuesday or after 5 p.m. simply because the river path is accessible.
fairmount-water-works.fees: General admission is free and donations are welcome. Groups of 10 or more must schedule in advance, with recommended group and tour donations published by the operator.
fairmount-water-works.accessibility: The operator currently reports no elevator access because of Hurricane Ida flood damage. Contact Water Works before a visit requiring elevator service or a specific exhibit route.
fairmount-water-works.dogs: Pets are not a normal fit inside the interpretive center. Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park paths where posted; confirm service-animal access with the operator.
fairmount-water-works.family: The turbine, watershed exhibits, short film and river setting can make a strong free family stop. Confirm the Wednesday-Saturday schedule and elevator limitation before arriving with a stroller or mobility need.
fairmount-water-works.need: Separate the free exhibits from the outdoor riverfront. Building access is limited to Wednesday-Saturday, and the elevator remains unavailable; flooding or city events can also affect Waterworks Drive.

smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.description: Smith Memorial Playground and Playhouse is a free 6.5-acre family destination with more than 50 outdoor play structures, a three-level indoor Playhouse and the Ann Newman Giant Wooden Slide.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.location: Navigate to 3500 Reservoir Drive in East Fairmount Park. Smith is about one-third mile inside the park from the 33rd Street and Oxford Street transit approach.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.parking: A free lot sits in front of the Playhouse. When it fills, the operator allows parking along Reservoir Drive; remove valuables and obey all posted restrictions.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.hours: April-September: Tuesday-Friday 10 a.m.-6 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 10 a.m.-7 p.m. October-March: Tuesday-Sunday 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Closed Mondays; weather may close all or part, and the Playhouse closes one hour before the Playground in spring and summer.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.restrooms: Restrooms are available as part of the staffed Playground and Playhouse visit. Do not rely on them before opening, after closing or during a weather closure.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.fees: Daily family visits are free. Advance reservations and fees apply to groups of more than 10 children, and rentals or special events are separate.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.accessibility: Smith describes inclusive indoor and outdoor play, but equipment and terrain vary by age and ability. Contact staff before visiting for a specific mobility, sensory or accommodation need.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.dogs: Animals are not permitted at Smith. ADA-defined service animals are welcome.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.family: Smith is designed especially for children age 10 and under. Children must remain with an adult, use age-appropriate equipment and stay within sight of their caregiver.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.need: Hours are weather permitting, the Playhouse can close before the outdoor playground, and food options nearby are limited. Bring food if needed, but grilling and barbecuing are prohibited.

shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.description: Shofuso is a ticketed 1.2-acre Japanese house and garden in West Fairmount Park, with timed entry, delicate historic interiors and separate visitor rules.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.address: Lansdowne Drive and Horticultural Drive, Philadelphia, PA 19131
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.sourceLabel: Japan America Society of Greater Philadelphia
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.location: Use the Shofuso pin inside the Centennial District near Lansdowne and Horticultural Drives. It is not the Horticulture Center entrance or the Please Touch Museum lot.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.parking: The operator lists free parking in the nearby lot. Capacity can tighten during Centennial District events, so reserve the timed visit before driving across the park.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.hours: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 11 a.m.-5 p.m. Entry is by timed ticket and capacity is limited; Shofuso operates rain or shine.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.restrooms: Plan restroom use around the staffed visit and nearby Centennial District facilities. Confirm current access when reserving, especially for a mobility or family need.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.fees: Published admission is $15 for adults and $10 for seniors, children 5-17, college students and teachers. SNAP/EBT and ACCESS admission is $2 for the cardholder plus up to four family members; listed member, military and museum-worker categories are free.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.accessibility: The operator says the historic house is not wheelchair or scooter accessible and is not easily accessible for walkers, canes or prosthetics. Rubber-tipped or softly covered mobility devices are permitted inside; contact staff before booking.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.dogs: Do not expect pets inside the house or garden. Confirm service-animal access and any accommodation directly before purchasing a timed ticket.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.family: The garden can be memorable for children who can move carefully around water, plants and fragile interiors. Timed capacity, house rules and the major mobility limitation should shape the visit.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.need: Reserve a timed ticket; capacity is limited and ordinary photoshoots are not permitted during open hours. The site is open rain or shine, but the historic house has significant mobility barriers.

please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.description: Please Touch Museum is the ticketed children's museum inside Memorial Hall, with interactive exhibits, a historic carousel, two floors of visitor services and its own parking and schedule.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.address: 4231 Avenue of the Republic, Philadelphia, PA 19131
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.location: Navigate to Memorial Hall at 4231 Avenue of the Republic in West Fairmount Park. The museum is separate from Shofuso, the Horticulture Center and Belmont Plateau even though all are in the Centennial District.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.parking: Use the museum's gated lot beside Memorial Hall and check the current parking charge when reserving. Designated accessible spaces are in the adjacent museum lot.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.hours: Closed Monday and Tuesday. Open Wednesday-Saturday 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; first, fourth and fifth Sundays 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; second and third Sundays 11 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Holiday and special-event hours differ, so verify the selected date.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.restrooms: Restrooms are available on both museum floors, with baby-changing stations in select restrooms. A nursing room is on the lower level behind the Creative Arts Studio.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.fees: Admission is ticketed, and reservations are encouraged for visitors and members age 12 months and older. Use the museum's current reservation page for admission, carousel and parking prices rather than an older listing.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.accessibility: The museum documents accessible parking, restrooms on both floors, a nursing room and sensory and accommodation programs. One complimentary personal-care-attendant admission is available on request for an eligible paid visitor or member.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.dogs: ADA-defined service animals are welcome. Emotional-support, comfort and therapy animals are not permitted inside.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.family: This is a purpose-built children's museum with interactive exhibits and a carousel. Reserve ahead, check the day's opening time and build in breaks for food, restrooms and sensory needs.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.need: Sunday opening time changes by week of the month, and holidays or events can override the weekly schedule. Make a reservation for faster entry and confirm current admission, carousel and parking charges.

valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.description: Valley Green Inn and Trailhead is the park's best-known creekside arrival, combining a historic restaurant, direct Forbidden Drive access, limited parking and one of Wissahickon's three permanent public restrooms.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.address: Valley Green Road at Wissahickon Creek, Philadelphia, PA 19128
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.sourceLabel: Friends of the Wissahickon visitor information
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.location: Navigate to the Valley Green Inn and lower trailhead pin on Valley Green Road beside Wissahickon Creek. This is a creek-level arrival on Forbidden Drive, not the upper Valley Green Road parking area.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.parking: Small public parking areas serve both sides of the Valley Green bridge and an upper lot sits farther up Valley Green Road. Spaces fill quickly; use only legal spaces, lock the vehicle and leave no valuables visible.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.hours: Use the trail during daylight under City trail rules. The restaurant, outdoor restroom and any event-controlled access keep their own schedules; confirm the inn directly if food or indoor service is essential.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.restrooms: Friends of the Wissahickon lists a permanent outdoor flushing restroom at Valley Green Inn. Because operating access can change, use it before heading away from the trailhead rather than assuming another restroom along the route.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.fees: Trailhead, bridge-view and Forbidden Drive access are free. Restaurant meals, private events and other services cost separately.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.accessibility: The arrival reaches broad gravel Forbidden Drive at creek level, but parking availability, gravel, bridge transitions and grades from the upper lot vary. Confirm a suitable space and current restroom access before a mobility-dependent trip.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on park trails under the City's six-foot rule. The restaurant and event areas may set separate animal rules; keep dogs clear of diners and narrow bridge traffic.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.family: This is a practical family starting point for a short creek walk because it combines a recognizable landmark, broad trail and restroom. Parking is tight and the creek is not a play or wading area.
valley-green-inn-and-trailhead.need: Valley Green is popular and can feel full even when other Wissahickon entrances are quiet. Arrive with a backup trailhead, protect valuables and separate park access from restaurant hours or reservations.

forbidden-drive.description: Forbidden Drive is Wissahickon's 5.35-mile broad gravel spine, following the creek through the gorge and connecting trailheads, historic landmarks and steeper color-blazed side trails.
forbidden-drive.sourceLabel: Friends of the Wissahickon maps and directions
forbidden-drive.location: Forbidden Drive extends through most of the park rather than occupying one point. Choose a segment and trailhead on the FOW map; Valley Green, Bells Mill, Northwestern Avenue and the Ridge Avenue end create very different outing lengths.
forbidden-drive.parking: There is no single Forbidden Drive lot. Park at a legal mapped trailhead and avoid Livezey Lane and Kitchen's Lane, which must remain clear for emergency access. Popular lots require a backup plan.
forbidden-drive.hours: City trail regulations open trails dawn to dusk, seven days a week. Curfew, storm damage, restoration work or an entrance closure may shorten access independently.
forbidden-drive.restrooms: Permanent restrooms are at Valley Green Inn, Kitchen's Lane at Forbidden Drive and the Wissahickon Environmental Center. Seasonal portable toilets appear at selected trailheads, but long sections of the route have no facility.
forbidden-drive.fees: Walking and running are free. Bicycle and equestrian permit rules apply to Upper Wissahickon soft trails; nonresident riders age 16 or older pay the published annual permit fee.
forbidden-drive.accessibility: FOW describes Forbidden Drive as gravel, 5.35 miles long, about 25 feet wide on average, with an average 3% grade and obstacles up to three inches. It is the park's most predictable route, but surface, drainage and trailhead transitions still vary.
forbidden-drive.dogs: Dogs are welcome on a leash no longer than six feet. Keep right, manage the leash around cyclists and horses, and pick up waste.
forbidden-drive.family: A short out-and-back from Valley Green or another mapped trailhead is easier than committing to the full route. Set a turnaround point, carry water and keep children out of the creek.
forbidden-drive.need: The route is shared by walkers, runners, bicycles and horses, with a seven-mile-per-hour trail speed limit and pedestrians holding right of way. Download the map before entering because cellular service is inconsistent.

devil-s-pool.description: Devil's Pool is a natural pool at the Cresheim Creek confluence, reached only by trail and best treated as a scenic waypoint because swimming, wading, jumping and vehicle access on Livezey Lane are prohibited.
devil-s-pool.address: Devil's Pool Trail, Wissahickon Valley Park, Philadelphia, PA 19119
devil-s-pool.sourceLabel: Friends of the Wissahickon visitor information
devil-s-pool.location: The pool lies off the trail near the confluence of Cresheim and Wissahickon Creeks, more than half a mile from the nearest legal trailhead. Follow the official map and remain on the marked approach.
devil-s-pool.parking: There is no legal parking or drop-off on Livezey Lane; it is emergency access. FOW recommends legal alternatives such as the Mt. Airy Avenue trailhead or Henry Avenue between the Summit and Wigard trailheads.
devil-s-pool.hours: Visit only during daylight trail hours and leave enough time for the return hike. Storms, high water, ice, erosion or restoration can close the approach even when the broader park is open.
devil-s-pool.restrooms: There is no restroom at Devil's Pool. Use one of the park's three permanent facilities before hiking, and remember that the nearest legal trailhead is more than half a mile away.
devil-s-pool.fees: Trail access is free. No ticket, reservation or paid activity authorizes swimming or vehicle access on Livezey Lane.
devil-s-pool.accessibility: The trail approach includes natural surfaces, rock, roots, grades and potentially slick edges; it is not a step-free destination. Limited cell service and the distance from emergency access increase the consequence of a fall.
devil-s-pool.dogs: Dogs must remain on a leash no longer than six feet and out of the water. Manage the leash carefully on rock, narrow approaches and crowded viewpoints.
devil-s-pool.family: This is not a splash pad or swimming hole. Families should choose it only for children able to manage the trail and follow water-edge rules; Forbidden Drive is a simpler first Wissahickon outing.
devil-s-pool.need: Swimming and wading are illegal and dangerous because of currents, submerged objects, water quality and wet rock. Do not jump, climb toward the water or block Livezey Lane, and carry all trash out.

thomas-mill-covered-bridge.description: Thomas Mill Covered Bridge is the only surviving covered bridge in the Wissahickon, a red pedestrian landmark beside Forbidden Drive reached as part of a trail outing rather than by driving across it.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.address: Thomas Mill Road Trail at Forbidden Drive, Philadelphia, PA 19118
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.location: The bridge crosses Wissahickon Creek near Forbidden Drive in the northern valley. Use the official park map to choose a trailhead and approach on foot, bicycle or permitted horse; the landmark is not a public motor-vehicle crossing.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.parking: There is no dedicated visitor lot at the bridge. Choose a legal mapped trailhead for the northern park, keep emergency routes clear and calculate the walk from that exact entrance before leaving.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.hours: Reach the bridge during daylight trail hours. High water, ice, fallen trees or trail work can affect the approach independently of the broader park curfew.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.restrooms: There is no public restroom at the bridge. Identify a permanent restroom at the Environmental Center, Kitchen's Lane or Valley Green before beginning the hike.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.fees: Viewing and crossing the bridge as part of a normal trail visit is free. Bicycle and equestrian permit rules may apply on connecting Upper Wissahickon soft trails.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.accessibility: The bridge is a trail landmark with gravel and natural-surface approaches; route and grade depend on the selected trailhead. Do not assume a step-free approach based only on the bridge deck.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the trail and bridge under the City's six-foot rule. Yield at the narrow covered span and keep pets away from horses and the creek edge.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.family: The red bridge makes a rewarding family landmark if the selected hike matches children's distance and terrain ability. Bring water, identify a restroom first and supervise at the creek.
thomas-mill-covered-bridge.need: Download the map and choose the complete out-and-back route before starting. The nearby historic fountain is sealed and is not a drinking-water source.

fingerspan.description: Fingerspan is Jody Pinto's 59-foot weathering-steel sculpture and footbridge on the Orange Trail, spanning a steep ravine reached by rocky trail and WPA stone stairs.
fingerspan.address: Orange Trail between Livezey Lane and Mt. Airy Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19119
fingerspan.location: Fingerspan sits on the Orange Trail between Livezey Lane and Mt. Airy Avenue, above a steep ravine. Follow the official trail map and blazes; it is not visible from a parking lot or Forbidden Drive.
fingerspan.parking: Use a legal mapped trailhead such as Mt. Airy Avenue and hike to the bridge. Do not use Livezey Lane for parking or drop-off because it is reserved for emergency access.
fingerspan.hours: Visit in daylight trail hours and leave time for the rocky return. The Orange Trail approach may close for erosion, fallen trees, ice or restoration even when Forbidden Drive remains open.
fingerspan.restrooms: There is no restroom at Fingerspan or on its immediate Orange Trail approach. Use a confirmed permanent facility before starting and carry what you need.
fingerspan.fees: The trail and public artwork are free to visit. No reservation is required for an ordinary hike.
fingerspan.accessibility: The destination is not step-free: its approach uses a narrow natural-surface trail, grades, rock and stone stairs, and the bridge has a grated deck over a deep ravine. Choose Forbidden Drive for a more predictable surface.
fingerspan.dogs: Dogs must stay on a leash no longer than six feet. Keep the leash short on stairs, the grated bridge and narrow trail, and yield to oncoming hikers.
fingerspan.family: Fingerspan can be memorable for experienced young hikers, but it is not a casual stroller outing. Children need close supervision on stone stairs, the grated span and steep terrain.
fingerspan.need: Download the map before entering and do not improvise a shortcut from Livezey Lane. Wet leaves, ice and low light make the stairs and rock approach substantially harder.

dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.description: Dilworth Park Fountain is a 241-jet, zero-depth water feature over the transit concourse, animated by Janet Echelman and OLIN's Pulse artwork with colored mist that follows subway movement below.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.location: The fountain occupies the broad central plaza on City Hall's west side, between the 15th Street transit headhouses and the Greenfield Lawn. Use the exact fountain pin rather than the larger City Hall complex.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.parking: There is no dedicated park parking. Arrive by SEPTA or use a paid Center City garage; curb spaces are limited and loading, construction or events can change nearby access.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.hours: The fountain operates seasonally from April through October, weather permitting. It may pause for maintenance, events or unsafe conditions even while Dilworth Park remains open from 6 a.m. to 1 a.m.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.restrooms: Public bathrooms are inside City Hall and their hours vary. There is no restroom in the fountain plaza, so confirm City Hall access before changing clothes or planning a long family visit.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.fees: Fountain and Pulse viewing is free. Food, drinks, ticketed programs and winter attractions cost separately.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.accessibility: The plaza has barrier-free street-level paths and the fountain is a flush, zero-depth surface. Wet paving can be slippery, and not every transit line below City Hall is yet fully accessible; choose the exact SEPTA entrance for the line you need.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.dogs: Dogs must remain on a leash no longer than six feet and stay out of the fountain. The adjacent Greenfield Lawn also excludes dogs.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.family: This is an urban water-play space rather than a fenced splash pad. Bring a change of clothes, supervise around moving pedestrians and wet paving, and identify an open City Hall restroom before play begins.
dilworth-park-fountain-and-pulse.need: Pulse mist and fountain jets are operational features, not guaranteed continuous performances. Check the operator's current park update and weather before making water play the purpose of a trip.

rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.description: Rothman Orthopaedics Ice Rink is Dilworth Park's seasonal outdoor skating rink, installed over the fountain plaza during the winter program and operated with timed sessions and separate admission.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.location: The rink replaces the central fountain footprint on the west side of City Hall. Enter from 15th Street and follow the current winter layout for admission, rentals and the session queue.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.parking: There is no rink lot. SEPTA is the simplest arrival; otherwise use a paid Center City garage and allow extra time for holiday traffic, event closures and limited curb access.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.hours: The rink generally operates from mid-November through late February, but daily sessions, holiday hours and weather closures change by season. Use the current winter schedule before traveling.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.restrooms: Public bathrooms are inside City Hall and hours vary. Winter structures may offer changing or service space but should not be treated as a guaranteed public restroom.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.fees: Skating and rentals are ticketed separately from free park access. Do not rely on a prior season's prices, discounts or reservation rules; check the current winter program when it is published.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.accessibility: Barrier-free plaza paths reach the rink perimeter. Contact the current operator before booking for adaptive skating, transfer needs or a non-skating companion accommodation because session procedures can change.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.dogs: Dogs may pass through permitted park areas on a six-foot leash but cannot enter the ice. Crowds, skate traffic and temporary winter structures make this a poor pet destination.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.family: Choose a session suited to the skaters' ability, reserve if the current season requires it and arrive early enough for check-in and rentals. Gloves and weather layers matter even on mild days.
rothman-orthopaedics-ice-rink.need: The rink does not operate year-round and can close for rain, warmth, ice maintenance or a private event. Confirm the same-day session before leaving and separate rink hours from the park's broader 6 a.m.-1 a.m. schedule.

albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.description: Albert M. Greenfield Lawn is Dilworth Park's 6,900-square-foot seasonal lawn and shaded seating area, transformed into the Wintergarden with plantings, lights and gathering space during the colder season.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.sourceLabel: Center City District 2026 Dilworth Park fact sheet
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.location: The lawn sits immediately north of the fountain on City Hall's west apron, near the Dilworth Park Cafe and tree groves. Seasonal installations can change its edges and entrances.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.parking: There is no dedicated lawn parking. Use SEPTA or a paid Center City garage and check for City Hall events that may restrict nearby streets or plaza access.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.hours: The park is open 6 a.m.-1 a.m., but the lawn is seasonal and can close for recovery, maintenance, private events or conversion to the Wintergarden. Programs keep their own published times.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.restrooms: Public bathrooms are inside City Hall and hours vary. Confirm access before settling in for a long visit, especially with children.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.fees: Ordinary lawn and Wintergarden access is free. Food, drinks, ticketed attractions and some special events are separate.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.accessibility: Barrier-free paved paths reach the lawn perimeter and seasonal garden. Grass, movable furniture, crowds and temporary event surfaces can be less predictable than the surrounding plaza.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.dogs: Dogs are not allowed on the Greenfield Lawn. Leashed dogs may use other permitted park paths, but temporary events can impose tighter controls.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.family: The lawn is useful for a short break near the fountain, while the Wintergarden offers a seasonal walk-through setting. It is not a fenced play area, so supervise children around plaza traffic and event equipment.
albert-m-greenfield-lawn-and-wintergarde.need: Do not assume the lawn is available because the park is open. Recovery periods and seasonal conversions can close the grass; check the current program if lawn seating is important.

dilworth-park-transit-entrances.description: Dilworth Park's glass transit headhouses and elevators connect the plaza to SEPTA's 15th Street Market-Frankford/Trolley station complex and the wider City Hall concourse, with accessibility differing by line and entrance.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.address: 15th Street and Market Street, Philadelphia, PA 19102
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.sourceLabel: SEPTA City Hall and 15th Street Station Accessibility Program
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.location: Use the glass headhouses and marked elevators along the park's 15th Street edge. Follow signs for the exact Market-Frankford, trolley or Broad Street service rather than assuming every entrance reaches every platform directly.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.parking: Transit is the intended arrival. If driving, use a paid Center City garage; the park has no public lot and curb access can be restricted by buses, loading, construction or events.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.hours: Station entrances follow SEPTA service and temporary closure schedules, not the park's 6 a.m.-1 a.m. hours. Verify the line and elevator status for the time of travel.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.restrooms: Do not expect a public restroom in the SEPTA concourse. Public bathrooms are inside City Hall with varying hours.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.fees: Entering the park is free; SEPTA fare is required beyond station fare lines. Use SEPTA's current fare information rather than an older listing.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.accessibility: The completed 15th Street work provides elevators for Market-Frankford and trolley access, while full Broad Street Line accessibility at City Hall remains an active SEPTA project. Check elevator status and the exact accessible route before traveling.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.dogs: Pets on SEPTA must follow the agency's current carrier and service-animal rules. A dog permitted on park paths is not automatically permitted aboard transit without meeting those rules.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.family: The direct transit arrival avoids parking, but the concourse is large and line transfers can be confusing. Decide the correct exit before boarding and keep children close around platforms, escalators and the busy plaza.
dilworth-park-transit-entrances.need: City Hall and 15th Street are connected but not uniformly accessible across every line. Use SEPTA's current concourse map and elevator alerts, and allow extra transfer time rather than choosing an entrance only because it is closest.

meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.description: Meadow Lake and the FDR Park Boathouse form the park's primary lake-view, fishing and program meeting area, with shoreline paths, no swimming and access that changes with flooding and restoration work.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.location: Use the boathouse and Meadow Lake pin inside the park loop, not the Broad Street gateway. The lake system is extensive, so decide whether the boathouse, a fishing program or a short shoreline walk is the actual destination.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.parking: Use a legal lot on the park loop nearest the boathouse. Parking is normally free, but Eagles games can trigger paid overflow parking and events, flooding or construction can change the approach.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.hours: Vehicle gates are open 6 a.m.-9 p.m. April-October and 6 a.m.-6 p.m. November-March. Fishing and boating programs keep published event times, and shoreline access may close after storms or during work.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.restrooms: The closest dependable permanent facility is outside the Welcome Center at 1800 Pattison Avenue; confirm its access before moving around the lake. The boathouse pavilion should not be assumed to provide an open public restroom.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.fees: Lake-edge walking and ordinary legal fishing access are free. Programs, permits, equipment or special events may use separate registration, although current community fishing and boating days advertise equipment at no cost.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.accessibility: The 2026 City picnic application says the FDR Boathouse Pavilion is not ADA compliant. Shoreline grades, older paving, mud and detours vary, so confirm the exact program meeting point and route before a mobility-dependent visit.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.dogs: Leashed dogs may use general park paths but should remain out of the water, habitat restoration areas and program equipment. Keep the leash short around anglers and narrow shoreline sections.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.family: A short lake walk or staffed family fishing program can work well, but this is open water with no swimming and no continuous barrier. Bring sun protection and supervise at every shoreline edge.
meadow-lake-and-fdr-park-boathouse.need: Swimming is prohibited. Check flooding and construction, do not launch or borrow equipment outside an authorized program, and leave enough time to exit before the seasonal vehicle gate closes.

fdr-park-skatepark.description: FDR Park Skatepark is the world-known DIY concrete skate environment beneath I-95, with bowls, transitions and an industrial setting that is separate from the park's playground and lake recreation areas.
fdr-park-skatepark.address: FDR Park beneath I-95, Philadelphia, PA 19145
fdr-park-skatepark.location: Navigate to the skatepark beneath I-95 on the park's eastern side. Do not follow the Anna C. Verna Playground pin; the skatepark has its own parking area and permanent restroom across the loop.
fdr-park-skatepark.parking: Use the legal lot beneath I-95 near the skatepark. The park identifies roughly 900 total spaces, but stadium events can impose fees or fill the nearest area and construction can alter circulation.
fdr-park-skatepark.hours: Use the skatepark within posted park access and seasonal vehicle-gate hours. Lighting, maintenance, events, flooding or work may shorten usable time; skating after dark should never be inferred from an open vehicle gate.
fdr-park-skatepark.restrooms: Friends of FDR Park identifies a permanent brick restroom across from the skatepark beneath I-95. Confirm that it is open before beginning a long session.
fdr-park-skatepark.fees: Ordinary public skatepark use is free. Lessons, events, vendors or organized programs may be separate.
fdr-park-skatepark.accessibility: The parking and spectator approach is developed, but the skate terrain itself is steep concrete designed for wheeled sport. Surface damage, debris, standing water and active riders create hazards independent of the access path.
fdr-park-skatepark.dogs: Keep leashed dogs outside active skate lines and away from bowls and ramps. Noise, wheels and confined movement make the riding area a poor pet setting.
fdr-park-skatepark.family: This is not a beginner playground. Helmets and appropriate protective equipment are strongly prudent, younger riders need close supervision, and spectators should remain clear of riding lines.
fdr-park-skatepark.need: Inspect the concrete and traffic pattern before entering, yield to active riders and do not treat the shaded highway setting as protection from lightning, flooding or severe weather.

american-swedish-historical-museum.description: The American Swedish Historical Museum is a separately operated, ticketed cultural destination inside FDR Park, with twelve galleries, its own Pattison Avenue entrance, museum hours and accessibility procedure.
american-swedish-historical-museum.location: Navigate to 1900 Pattison Avenue, west of the main Broad Street park gateway. Use the museum entrance rather than a general FDR Park or picnic-grove pin.
american-swedish-historical-museum.parking: The museum lists accessible parking along Pattison Avenue by its rear entrance. Construction for planned access improvements or a park event can alter the approach, so use current museum directions rather than an old event parking map.
american-swedish-historical-museum.hours: Public hours are Tuesday-Sunday, 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; the museum is normally closed Monday and on listed holidays. Special tours, events and 2026 centennial programming can override the weekly pattern.
american-swedish-historical-museum.restrooms: Restrooms are available to museum visitors during staffed public hours. Do not depend on indoor access before opening, after closing or when the museum is closed for a holiday or private event.
american-swedish-historical-museum.fees: Current general admission is $15 adults, $10 seniors, students and military, $5 ages 5-11, and free under age 5; ACCESS admission is $2 for adults and children over 5. The second Sunday of each month is listed as free, but verify current terms.
american-swedish-historical-museum.accessibility: Accessible parking is along Pattison Avenue at the rear entrance; ring the doorbell for admittance. Caregivers accompanying visitors with special needs do not pay admission. Planned access construction may change the route.
american-swedish-historical-museum.dogs: ADA-defined service dogs are welcome. Emotional-support, comfort and therapy animals are not permitted inside.
american-swedish-historical-museum.family: The galleries and scheduled family programs offer an indoor complement to the park. Check the current exhibition and event calendar, admission and bag policy before arriving with a group.
american-swedish-historical-museum.need: The museum is not open on the park's full schedule. Large bags are prohibited in galleries, lockers are on the lower level, and there is no general food or beverage service onsite.

olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.description: Olmsted Overlook and its historic gazebo are a recognizable lake-side gathering landmark in FDR Park, used for views, informal rest and scheduled free music rather than as a staffed visitor center.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.address: FDR Park loop near Meadow Lake, Philadelphia, PA 19145
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.sourceLabel: Friends of FDR Park public programs
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.location: Use the gazebo and Olmsted Overlook pin beside the lake system inside the park loop. It is separate from the boathouse, museum and Broad Street gateway, even though event directions may use those larger landmarks.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.parking: Choose a legal loop lot near the overlook and leave the event area clear for permitted setup. Stadium events, markets and construction can redirect traffic or impose a parking fee.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.hours: The outdoor landmark follows park and seasonal vehicle-gate access. Scheduled programs have their own times; Friends currently lists Not Just Jazz at the Gazebo/Olmsted Overlook on alternating Tuesdays from June through October, weather permitting.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.restrooms: There is no guaranteed restroom at the gazebo. Identify the permanent facility outside the Welcome Center or across from the skatepark before settling in for a program.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.fees: Ordinary overlook and gazebo access is free, and the listed Not Just Jazz series is free. Private reservations, vendors and other events may have separate requirements.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.accessibility: The overlook is reached from the park loop, but older paving, lawn, curb transitions, event furniture and wet conditions vary. Confirm the event's accessible approach before relying on a seat or drop-off location.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the surrounding general park area unless an event posts a restriction. Keep pets away from performers, food trucks, crowded seating and the lake edge.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.family: The gazebo is a useful family landmark and free-music setting, but it is not a playground or fenced space. Bring seating when advised and supervise children near roads and water.
olmsted-overlook-and-gazebo.need: This is an unstaffed outdoor landmark. Confirm the exact program date and weather status, bring a chair or blanket when appropriate and do not assume food, restrooms or shelter will be available.

rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.description: The central plaza and reflecting pool are the square's primary meeting place, where four diagonal walks converge among benches, lawns and the historic Paul Cret landscape.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.address: Rittenhouse Square central plaza, Philadelphia, PA 19103
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.location: Enter from any corner and follow the broad diagonal walk to the center. This is the easiest meeting point, but it is distinct from the Children's Pool and sculpture locations toward the southwest interior.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.parking: There is no park lot. Use transit or a paid Center City garage and walk to the nearest corner; do not circle the square expecting visitor parking beside the plaza.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.hours: The plaza follows the City's 10 p.m. park curfew. Pool operation, cleaning, lawn recovery, performances and permitted events may use shorter schedules or temporarily occupy the center.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.restrooms: There is no documented standalone park restroom at the plaza. Identify a confirmed-open nearby facility before meeting here for a long visit.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.fees: Ordinary plaza, bench and reflecting-pool viewing are free. Permitted programs, nearby food and market purchases may cost separately.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.accessibility: Paved diagonal walks reach the center from all four corners, but historic paving, crowds, furniture, wet leaves, snow, ice and event setup can narrow the usable route.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the general paths under City rules. Keep pets out of the water, off recovering lawns and controlled around seating, children and food.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.family: The pool and broad plaza make a simple family landmark, but this is not a fenced splash pad or playground. Supervise children around water and on every route back to the surrounding streets.
rittenhouse-square-central-plaza-and-ref.need: The pool is ornamental, not a swimming or wading destination. Check the live event calendar and expect the center to be busiest at lunch, on pleasant weekends and during permitted programs.

lion-crushing-a-serpent.description: Lion Crushing a Serpent is Antoine-Louis Barye's dramatic bronze, created in 1832 and cast in 1891, and the first sculpture installed in Rittenhouse Square.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.address: Rittenhouse Square southwest interior, Philadelphia, PA 19103
lion-crushing-a-serpent.location: Look in the southwest portion of the square between the central plaza and the 19th Street side. Use the exact sculpture pin rather than searching the full perimeter.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.parking: The sculpture has no separate parking. Arrive by transit, walking or a paid garage and enter from the southwest or nearest available corner.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.hours: View it during ordinary park access before the 10 p.m. curfew. Conservation work, fencing, snow or an event may temporarily limit close approach.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.restrooms: There is no restroom at the sculpture and no documented standalone park restroom. Plan a nearby confirmed-open facility.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.accessibility: Use the paved park walks, then assess the final approach around benches, plantings and historic surfaces. Do not cross closed lawn or conservation barriers for a closer view.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.dogs: Leashed dogs are permitted on general paths but should remain away from the bronze and landscaping.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.family: The lion makes an engaging stop on a short sculpture hunt. Children should view rather than climb the artwork and remain close around busy paths.
lion-crushing-a-serpent.need: This is protected public art, not play equipment. Pair it with Duck Girl and Billy for a compact walking loop, and respect any temporary conservation enclosure.

duck-girl.description: Duck Girl is Paul Manship's 1911 bronze figure at the Children's Pool, a small fountain setting in the square's southwest interior rather than a water-play area.
duck-girl.address: Children's Pool, Rittenhouse Square, Philadelphia, PA 19103
duck-girl.location: Find the Children's Pool in the southwest interior, a short walk from the central plaza. It is separate from the large central reflecting pool.
duck-girl.parking: There is no destination parking. Use transit or a paid garage, then approach through the nearest southwest entrance.
duck-girl.hours: The artwork follows ordinary park access and the 10 p.m. curfew. Water operation and close access may stop for weather, maintenance or conservation.
duck-girl.restrooms: There is no restroom at the Children's Pool. Use a confirmed-open nearby facility before arriving with young children.
duck-girl.accessibility: Paved park paths lead near the pool, but historic edging, wet surfaces, crowds and temporary barriers can affect the final approach.
duck-girl.dogs: Keep leashed dogs out of the pool and away from the sculpture, children and planting beds.
duck-girl.family: The child-and-duck figure is a good family art stop, but the pool is ornamental and the bronze is not climbing equipment. Maintain hands-on supervision near water and streets.
duck-girl.need: Do not confuse the Children's Pool name with a public swimming or splash facility. View the artwork without entering the water or touching the bronze.

billy.description: Billy is Albert Laessle's 1914 bronze goat, modeled after a family goat and now one of Rittenhouse Square's best-known child-friendly public-art landmarks.
billy.address: Rittenhouse Square southwest side, Philadelphia, PA 19103
billy.location: Look along the southwest side of the square near the sculpture cluster and Children's Pool. The exact pin is more useful than the park's center point.
billy.parking: Billy has no separate parking or drop-off. Use transit or a paid garage and enter from the nearest southwest corner.
billy.hours: View the outdoor sculpture during ordinary square access before the 10 p.m. curfew. Maintenance, conservation or event fencing may restrict approach.
billy.restrooms: There is no restroom at the sculpture and no documented standalone public restroom in the square.
billy.accessibility: Use the paved path network and respect lawn or planting closures. Crowds gathering around the small bronze can make the immediate area tight for mobility devices.
billy.dogs: Keep leashed dogs controlled and away from the artwork, nearby children and plantings.
billy.family: Billy is a memorable stop for children on a sculpture walk, but the bronze is public art rather than playground equipment. Take turns around other visitors and keep children away from street exits.
billy.need: Visit Billy as part of a short loop with Duck Girl and Lion Crushing a Serpent. Do not climb, mark or attach anything to the bronze.

franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.description: The restored 1838 Franklin Square Fountain and nearby SquareBurger form the park's central gathering area, with free viewing but separate show and food-service schedules.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.sourceLabel: Historic Philadelphia Franklin Square visit guide
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.location: Enter at 6th and Race and follow the main paths to the central fountain. SquareBurger is nearby, but food pickup and fountain viewing use different queues during events.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.parking: There is no dedicated free park lot. Use PATCO, nearby SEPTA or a paid garage; festival nights create the greatest parking pressure.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.hours: Fountain shows are currently listed April 18-October 31, while SquareBurger is listed from noon to park closing during the published summer season. Both are weather dependent and the park is cleared at 5 p.m. on lantern-festival dates.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.restrooms: The expanded 2025 restrooms include accessible stalls and a separate gender-neutral family restroom. Access follows current park operations.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.fees: Fountain viewing is free during ordinary daytime access. Food and the ticketed evening lantern festival cost separately.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.accessibility: Main paths reach the fountain and new accessible restrooms, but queues, movable seating, wet paving and festival installations can narrow circulation.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.dogs: Leashed pets may use green spaces but should remain away from food service and fountain water; service-animal rules apply inside restricted attractions.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.family: The fountain, nearby playground, food and restrooms make this the easiest family meeting zone. Supervise around water and crowded paths.
franklin-square-fountain-and-squareburge.need: The fountain is not a splash pad. Check the live show calendar, weather and event access, and do not assume SquareBurger operates whenever the grounds are open.

parx-liberty-carousel.description: Parx Liberty Carousel is Franklin Square's gentle, ticketed family ride with Philadelphia-themed animals, separate operating hours and a rider-height supervision rule.
parx-liberty-carousel.address: Franklin Square, 200 N. 6th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19106
parx-liberty-carousel.sourceLabel: Historic Philadelphia Franklin Square visit guide
parx-liberty-carousel.location: The carousel sits inside the compact park loop near the fountain. Follow attraction signs rather than a street address once inside the square.
parx-liberty-carousel.parking: Use transit or a paid garage; the ride has no separate parking or drop-off lane.
parx-liberty-carousel.hours: Carousel hours follow the published seasonal park-attraction calendar and are weather dependent. Lantern-festival dates split free daytime access from ticketed evening access.
parx-liberty-carousel.restrooms: Use the park's expanded restrooms during operating hours; there is no restroom on the ride platform.
parx-liberty-carousel.fees: Current tickets are $4 for riders age three and older; children two and under ride free. Verify prices before visiting.
parx-liberty-carousel.accessibility: Ask staff about the current boarding and transfer procedure. The path approach is developed, but the moving ride and animal seats require individual assessment.
parx-liberty-carousel.dogs: Except for service animals, pets are not permitted on the carousel.
parx-liberty-carousel.family: Children under 42 inches must ride with a responsible adult. Keep children behind ride barriers until staff invite boarding.
parx-liberty-carousel.need: A park entrance or festival ticket does not automatically include a carousel ride. Confirm attraction hours, weather status and the correct ticket.

philly-mini-golf.description: Philly Mini Golf is Franklin Square's 18-hole outdoor course built around miniature Philadelphia landmarks, with timed capacity, separate tickets and weather-sensitive play.
philly-mini-golf.address: Franklin Square, 200 N. 6th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19106
philly-mini-golf.location: Find the gated mini-golf course inside the park loop. Check in at the attraction entrance rather than at the fountain or carousel queue.
philly-mini-golf.parking: There is no mini-golf lot. PATCO, SEPTA or a paid garage avoids circling the square.
philly-mini-golf.hours: Published 2026 hours vary by date and shorten to 10 a.m.-5 p.m. from June 5-August 16 before lantern-festival operations. Weather can stop play.
philly-mini-golf.restrooms: Use the park's expanded restrooms during operating hours; leave enough time before a timed or closing round.
philly-mini-golf.fees: Current prices are $15 adults and $12 children ages 3-13; children two and under are free with a paid guardian. Art-Reach Access Card restrictions apply.
philly-mini-golf.accessibility: The outdoor course has developed paths, but individual holes, obstacles, queues and temporary event layouts vary. Ask staff about the most workable route.
philly-mini-golf.dogs: Except for service animals, pets are not permitted in Philly Mini Golf.
philly-mini-golf.family: The course works best for children able to wait turns and remain within the playing lane. Younger children need close supervision around clubs and neighboring groups.
philly-mini-golf.need: Tickets are valid only during public operating hours. Check weather and festival transitions before starting a late round.

franklin-square-patco-station.description: Franklin Square PATCO Station reopened in 2025 beside the park, restoring direct rail access between Center City, Camden County and the square.
franklin-square-patco-station.location: Use the station headhouse beside Franklin Square and confirm the direction before passing the fare line. It is distinct from SEPTA's 5th and 8th Street stations.
franklin-square-patco-station.parking: The station is a transit arrival, not a park-and-ride. Use an origin station with appropriate parking or a paid Philadelphia garage if driving into Center City.
franklin-square-patco-station.hours: Train service follows PATCO's current timetable and service alerts, not park or attraction hours. Weeknight closures or maintenance can change service.
franklin-square-patco-station.restrooms: Do not depend on a public station restroom. The park's restrooms follow park operating hours and may be unavailable after closure.
franklin-square-patco-station.fees: PATCO fare is required. Park entry remains free during ordinary daytime access; attractions and events are separate.
franklin-square-patco-station.accessibility: The rebuilt station includes elevator access, but check live elevator and service status before a mobility-dependent trip.
franklin-square-patco-station.dogs: Pets and service animals must follow PATCO's current rules; park permission does not automatically permit ordinary pets aboard trains.
franklin-square-patco-station.family: The direct stop minimizes walking, but keep children close around fare gates, stairs, elevators and platforms and identify the correct direction before boarding.
franklin-square-patco-station.need: A train may operate when the square is closed or ticketed. Check both PATCO service and Franklin Square access for the return trip.

schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.description: The 2,000-foot Schuylkill Banks Boardwalk carries the trail over the river from Locust Street to South Street on a 15-foot-wide path with four widened overlooks.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.address: Schuylkill Banks Boardwalk at Locust Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.location: Approach from Locust Street at the north end or the South Street Bridge ramp at the south end. Walnut Street is the more useful central arrival when a restroom or staffed dock matters.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.parking: The Boardwalk has no lot. Choose a paid Center City garage or legal meter near Walnut, Locust or South Street before driving; the official map identifies options, and event or construction conditions can change the closest route.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.hours: Use the Boardwalk during trail hours from dawn to dusk. It may close independently for flooding, ice, repairs or work beneath nearby bridges even when other Schuylkill Banks sections remain open.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.restrooms: The nearest documented public facility is on the trail just south of Walnut Street, normally open daily from 9 a.m.-5 p.m. subject to staff availability. There is no restroom on the over-water span.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.fees: Walking, running, cycling and overlook use are free. Parking, tours, food and special programs cost separately.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.accessibility: The Boardwalk is a developed 15-foot-wide path with four widened overlooks. Approaches are paved, but mixed traffic, temporary barriers, wet surfaces, ice and crowds can reduce maneuvering space.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the Boardwalk under the six-foot City rule; keep the leash short and the animal out of bicycle and running traffic. Off-leash use is not allowed here.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.family: The skyline and river overlooks make a memorable short family route. Keep children beside an adult rather than spread across the travel lane, and supervise continuously at the open river edge.
schuylkill-banks-boardwalk.need: This is a transportation path as well as an overlook. Keep right, step fully into a widened area before stopping, pass only when clear and never bypass a closure barrier over the river.

walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.description: The Walnut Street hub combines a central trail entrance, the corridor's staffed restroom and a gated dock used for guided tours and limited small-watercraft access.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.address: Schuylkill River Trail at Walnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.sourceLabel: Schuylkill Banks official map and boating guide
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.location: Descend from Walnut Street to the east-bank trail and look just south of the bridge for the restroom and dock area. This is north of the Boardwalk's Locust Street over-water section.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.parking: There is no dedicated dock lot. Use a paid garage, legal meter or transit near Walnut Street and allow extra time to bring nonmotorized equipment down the approved approach without blocking the trail.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.hours: The trail follows dawn-to-dusk use. The restroom is normally 9 a.m.-5 p.m. subject to staffing; the dock gate is opened by staff only when no scheduled program is using it, and guided tours follow reserved departure times.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.restrooms: A staffed public restroom sits just south of Walnut Street and is normally open daily from 9 a.m.-5 p.m., subject to staff availability. Use it before a tour because outdoor access does not guarantee the building is open.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.fees: Trail and restroom access are free. Guided kayak and riverboat programs have separate reservations and prices; bringing a small nonmotorized craft does not create unlimited dock access.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.accessibility: The paved trail reaches the hub, but the dock and watercraft transfer are separate physical tasks. Contact the program operator before booking for boarding, transfer or adaptive-paddling requirements.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.dogs: Short-leashed dogs may use the trail but are not automatically accepted on tours, at the gated dock or in watercraft. Keep pets clear of loading activity and moving bicycles.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.family: The restroom and central access make this a practical family meeting point. Guided kayak participants must be at least 12; anyone under 18 must be accompanied by an adult, and the operator asks guests to arrive 15 minutes early.
walnut-street-trail-hub-and-dock.need: There is no public motorized launch. When the dock is not reserved, staff may permit small-watercraft use for up to 30 minutes while users remain in sight; never climb a locked gate or assume access without staff.

south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.description: The South Street Bridge trail ramp is the ADA-accessible connection on the bridge's northeast side linking street level to the Boardwalk and east-bank river trail.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.address: South Street Bridge northeast side, Philadelphia, PA 19146
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.location: Use the northeast corner of the South Street Bridge and follow the signed ramp down to the trail. Do not navigate to the west bank or the bridge midpoint when seeking the Boardwalk connection.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.parking: The ramp has no parking. Use transit, walk from nearby neighborhoods or select legal paid parking before arrival; do not stop on the bridge or block the ramp for loading.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.hours: Use the ramp during trail hours from dawn to dusk. Maintenance, ice, flooding or bridge work can close the connection independently; follow any signed alternate rather than using stairs or a work zone.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.restrooms: There is no restroom at the ramp. The documented Schuylkill Banks restroom is farther north just south of Walnut Street and normally operates 9 a.m.-5 p.m. subject to staff availability.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.fees: The ramp, Boardwalk and trail are free. Parking and any reserved programs are separate.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.accessibility: The operator identifies this as an ADA-accessible ramp. Its long slope, turns, mixed users and weather exposure still matter; check for closures and allow others room to pass.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the ramp, but keep them close at switchbacks and away from bicycle wheels. Off-leash use is not allowed.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.family: The ramp is a useful stroller approach to the Boardwalk. Keep children to one side through turns and away from the bridge roadway and river edge.
south-street-bridge-trail-ramp.need: Walk your bicycle on the ramp. Riders mounting on the slope create conflicts at narrow turns; remount only after reaching the main trail and checking for approaching traffic.

hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.description: The free hammock grove and adjacent Lazy Hammock stage-and-bar area form Spruce Street Harbor Park's central gathering zone, with first-come seating and separate event and beverage schedules.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.address: 301 S. Christopher Columbus Boulevard, Philadelphia, PA 19106
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.location: Enter from Spruce Street and Columbus Boulevard and follow the park paths into the tree-covered hammock core. The Lazy Hammock performance area is inside the same compact zone; it is not RiverRink farther north.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.parking: There is no hammock-specific lot, and CAP construction limits on-site parking. Walk, bike, use transit or rideshare when possible; if driving, choose a current waterfront garage before leaving.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.hours: Use the hammocks during 2026 park hours: Sunday-Thursday 11 a.m.-10 p.m. and Friday-Saturday 11 a.m.-11 p.m., subject to weather and special holiday hours. Lazy Hammock programs and bar service follow separate schedules and close earlier.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.restrooms: Use the seasonal public restroom at the Spruce Street Harbor Park information center during operations. Go before the site closes; RiverRink and Cherry Street Pier facilities are separate destinations with separate hours.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.fees: General admission and ordinary first-come hammocks are free. Food, drinks, reserved gatherings and separately operated activities cost extra.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.accessibility: Primary park circulation is developed and DRWC describes its parks as ADA-compliant, but conventional hammocks require a transfer and may not suit every visitor. Adirondack chairs, picnic tables and lounge seating offer alternatives, subject to availability.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in the park but are not permitted in hammocks or on the barge. Keep pets clear of food lines, stages and crowded seating areas.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.family: Hammocks and daytime programming are family-friendly, but each hammock is limited to two people or 250 pounds. Supervise mounting and dismounting, do not let children swing into paths, and expect a more adult atmosphere around evening bar programming.
hammock-grove-and-lazy-hammock.need: All free seating is first-come, first-served, so a visit does not guarantee a hammock. Do not reserve unattended seats; check weather and the event calendar, and use conventional seating if a safe hammock transfer is not workable.

christopher-columbus-memorial.description: The Christopher Columbus Memorial is a permanent 1992 public artwork by Venturi Scott Brown inside Spruce Street Harbor Park and a compact landmark amid the seasonal attractions.
christopher-columbus-memorial.address: Spruce Street Harbor Park, 301 S. Christopher Columbus Boulevard, Philadelphia, PA 19106
christopher-columbus-memorial.location: Use the exact memorial pin inside the park near the Spruce Street arrival rather than searching along the full length of Christopher Columbus Boulevard. It stands within the seasonal park footprint.
christopher-columbus-memorial.parking: The memorial has no separate parking or drop-off. Follow current Harbor Park arrival guidance and avoid CAP construction closures; transit, walking and biking are usually simpler.
christopher-columbus-memorial.hours: View the outdoor memorial during published Harbor Park hours in season. Construction, events or maintenance can restrict its immediate surroundings even when the rest of the park remains open.
christopher-columbus-memorial.restrooms: The seasonal park information-center restroom is the relevant public facility during operations. There is no restroom at the artwork itself.
christopher-columbus-memorial.fees: Outdoor viewing is free. Parking, food, boats and other attractions are separate.
christopher-columbus-memorial.accessibility: Developed park paths approach the memorial, but event furnishings, queues and temporary barriers can change the final circulation space. Follow the open paved route and do not cross construction fencing.
christopher-columbus-memorial.dogs: Leashed dogs may accompany visitors in ordinary open park areas, subject to posted restrictions. Keep pets away from the artwork and nearby crowds.
christopher-columbus-memorial.family: The memorial can be a short public-art stop rather than a child-focused attraction. Keep children off the structure and supervise around adjacent paths and the waterfront.
christopher-columbus-memorial.need: This is a memorial, not play equipment or seating. Its subject can prompt different reactions; visit respectfully, do not climb it, and use the park's current map and signs if an event changes access.
